title: 0% VAT on Electricity Bills Explained (Oct 2026)
description: VAT on household electricity in Great Britain is 0% from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027. Who gets it, whether fixed tariffs are covered and what happens next.
h1: 0% VAT on electricity: what it means for your bill
intro: Household electricity in England, Scotland and Wales has a temporary zero rate of VAT until 31 March 2027. Here’s how it works.

image.alt: A smart thermostat on a wall

cardText: Who gets the VAT cut, fixed tariffs and when it ends.

sources.title: Ofgem: energy price cap will rise by 4% from October 2026

sections.html:
• Announced on 21 July 2026; applies from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027.
  • Covers electricity for domestic use in Great Britain. It does not apply in Northern Ireland.
  • Gas and other domestic fuels stay at 5% VAT.
  • It’s applied automatically by your supplier, including on fixed tariffs.
  • The government estimates a typical household saves around £45 a year.

sections.h2: What the 0% VAT rate means for a bill that spans 1 October
sections.html:
Many bills cover a period that started before 1 October 2026. HMRC’s guidance for suppliers says the VAT treatment can be based on when the energy was used, and recommends using meter readings to split the supply between the old 5% rate and the new 0% rate, though other fair and reasonable methods are allowed (as of November 2026). In practice, a bill that straddles the date may show two VAT lines, or a single blended figure.

Accurate readings make that split fairer, so submit one around 1 October if you can: see how to read your gas and electricity meter. If your bill looks wrong, our guide on how to complain to your energy supplier sets out the steps.

Unless the government extends it, VAT on household electricity goes back to 5% on 1 April 2027. That would push electricity prices up by about 5% on that date, on top of any change in the price cap. Keep an eye on our what’s changing calendar.

faqs.q: Does the 0% VAT rate apply to gas?
faqs.a: No. HMRC says other fuel types are not affected, so household gas stays at 5% VAT.

faqs.q: Does the 0% VAT on electricity apply in Northern Ireland?
faqs.a: No. It covers Great Britain only; qualifying electricity in Northern Ireland stays at the 5% reduced rate.

faqs.q: When does 0% VAT on electricity end?
faqs.a: The temporary zero rate runs from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027. Unless it is extended, the 5% rate returns on 1 April 2027.
